changes.walking: Admit native slow-movement candidates outside idle velocity. Keep an independent distance-driven walking phase for off-ball movement; do not restart it when a native candidate is requeued. Generate overlapping two-leg IK support along the actual local travel vector, including sideways/backward travel. Blend entry/exit in the simulation pose and apply that solved pose to the rendered skeleton. On-ball actions retain native event phase/contact gates and full-stick/RB speeds.
changes.visible_support: Transmit the solver pelvis translation and root rotation to the final rendered pose, rather than only applying individual limb deltas. A committed recovery step uses its exact solved pose through a gradual envelope. Actual final render ankle positions and torso direction are now measured at a bounded telemetry rate for human and CPU, not inferred from an IK counter.
changes.receiving: An eligible closest nearby CPU receiver can react when possession designation still points to a more distant teammate. Forecast finite adjustment steps up to 1.2 seconds; keep native actions and skin contact acceptance. Record the actor ID for the real upper-only chest contact so reception evidence identifies the actual receiving actor.
changes.impact: Every real swept body contact, including formerly unclassified body parts, transmits measured ball momentum to the body and a damped integrated upper-body reflex. Repeated skin hits do not restart a phase envelope and suppress the reaction. Real native receipt momentum also reaches the body. The learned tracker remains active for CPU reception even when the CPU is stationary, and impact response can continue during another action without moving the planned contact foot/head.
changes.fallen_contacts: Continue the moving-skin ball sweep while the actor is falling/getting up. Deliver subsequent real collision impulses to the articulated torso instead of discarding them while already falling.
changes.laboratory: H+F4/F5/F6 in the match arranges ground/chest/high deliveries to an actual CPU teammate. H+Ctrl+Shift+F4 places the ball safely inside the opposite half for an off-ball walking comparison. Fixtures only arrange positions/trajectories; they do not grant possession, select contact outcomes or replace the real CPU controller.

learned_motor.algorithm: cross-entropy neural policy search on perturbed angular dynamics
learned_motor.scope: Learned upper-body angular servo with native motion references and domain-randomized reduced dynamics. Not Euphoria, AMP, a trained whole-body locomotion/balance policy, or proof of full-body sim-to-game transfer.

failed_checks.check: reachable hold transmits reciprocal limited traction and slows escape

superseded_test_outcomes.reason: The sustained calm-hold fixture began during the native turn caused by F11 changing possession. A genuine shirt contact released at 40 ms when the hand exceeded its real reach. The fixture now lets that possession-induced turn settle for 800 ms before measuring the sustained hold, without changing the game binary or any acquisition/release/force/slowdown/escape threshold. The final trial sustains a real hold for 2.37 seconds and releases through actual escape.

investigated_findings: A solo with-ball speed test passed while actual off-ball walking was excluded by incoming velocity and directional candidate filters. The new test uses real medium-strength analog input in a 22-player match and observes actual final rendered ankles, complete swing, support and stance drift at three pressures.

Requeuing a native movement clip reset its slow gait pose while the root kept travelling. The new off-ball reference phase advances by actual distance and is independent of those requeues. The native movement/root and ball action selection still control responsiveness.

The first off-ball laboratory placed the ball beyond the touchline, legitimately triggering a restart and repositioning the human. The final fixture keeps the ball on the pitch; a new displacement assertion detects teleporting instead of excluding stopped frames.

Exact modulo-40 timestamp telemetry undersampled rendered poses because render timestamps are not exact simulation multiples. Bounded elapsed-time sampling now records the final pose consistently. Match coverage filters the actual 22 players instead of rejecting the three rendered referee actors.

A chest layer was visibly receiving but omitted actor ID in its real contact event. Add its actor field; the new reception checks identify both native and upper-layer skin contacts rather than mistakenly counting a later foot contact.
Ctrl+Alt+Fn can be intercepted as a system shortcut. The CPU delivery fixture uses H+Fn and is verified without overriding system shortcuts.

A phase-based reflex restarted on repeated hits and could suppress its own attack. The damped state integrates toward measured impact direction with bounded velocity/acceleration and decays after the impact.
No additional external motion captures, proprietary Euphoria implementation or new whole-body learned policy were added. Existing generated profiles are not counted as newly authored animations.
limits: Windows is cross-compiled and package/import-validated. Graphical tests run on Linux/X11 with a virtual Xbox controller; physical Windows controller feel/rendering still needs the user PC.
The learned model is a six-unit 18-weight upper-body angular servo, not a trained whole-body gait, reinforcement-learning humanoid or Euphoria. Footstep planning and IK remain analytical.

Rendered regression scenarios verify concrete trajectories/poses and limits; they do not guarantee every reception, universal nonpenetration, perfect anatomy or human-equivalent movement in every match situation.

Native animation still owns football actions and normal/full-stick/sprint selection. Foot support can release for actions, reach limits, held bodies or loss of balance. The controlled-ground-dribble collision exemption remains.
All 35 release scenarios below use the same final native hash. Earlier preflights are excluded from the release pass count.
